newsitem.title: JAPAN: Letter to 'Walter Mondale' undeliverable in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Letter to 'Walter Mondale' undeliverable in Japan.

text.p: A message in a bottle might have stood a better chance.

While it probably will not cause a new rift in U.S.-Japan relations, Japanese postal authorities are slightly embarrassed after mail apparently intended for former U.S. ambassador and vice president Walter Mondale recently turned up as undeliverable.

A letter addressed to "Walter F. Mondale" was included in a recent list showing foreigners with mail who could not be found. The list, usually of about 50 to 60 items, appears three times each month in Tokyo's English-language newspapers.
The letter was sent by air mail from the United States and classified as "undeliverable" because of an inaccurate address written on it, an official at Tokyo's International Post Office said.
The letter had been at the post office for about two months, the official said.
The U.S. embassy said it was unaware of the letter and had not seen the name of the former ambassador on the list.
"Those who know Mr. Mondale well certainly know that he is no longer in Japan," a spokeswoman for the U.S. embassy said.
After three years as U.S. ambassador, Mondale left in December.
The post office said it was not even sure that the mail was meant for the former ambassador.
"It may simply be that it is someone with the same name," the post office official said.
The English-language Tokyo phone book has only one Mondale, with his address listed as the U.S. Embassy in central Tokyo.
The mystery may never be solved. If no one picks up the letter soon, it will be returned to the sender.
